system.name: Aurora Support Resolution Agent
system.owner: D. Okafor, Director of Customer Operations
system.purpose: Resolve tier-1 customer support tickets end to end without analyst involvement, including issuing account credits under a fixed threshold.
system.model_provider: OpenAI GPT-4o via vendor SaaS platform

likelihood.label: High
drivers: agent ingests content it does not control - prompt injection surface (+2)
Training/retention use of submitted data unknown
Can send outbound communications containing processed data
External provider in scope: Aurora AI Inc.
Sensitive or personal data leaves the organisation
No completed AI-specific vendor risk assessment
Provider supports a high-impact business process

methodology.formula: Risk Score = Impact (1-4) x Likelihood (1-4) x Exposure (1-4), range 1-64

findings.title: Least privilege for AI agent tool access
findings.finding: Role-based access is in place, but the agent retains destructive or transactional permissions that are not scoped to individual tasks.
findings.business_impact: Limits what an incorrect classification can change to the ticket itself.
findings.recommendation: Replace the shared support application role with an agent-specific role scoped to the tier-1 queue: read ticket, append public comment, set status. Remove write access to customer account records.

findings.title: Human approval for high-impact agent actions
findings.finding: The agent performs high-impact actions with no human approval gate at any point in the flow.
findings.business_impact: Stops incorrect credits and inappropriate replies from reaching customers.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit human approval for any account credit and for the first outbound reply on a ticket.

findings.title: Prompt injection resistance and input validation
findings.finding: The agent ingests content it does not control, holds broad permissions and requires no approval. Injected instructions in that content could drive real actions.
findings.business_impact: Business impact not generated for this finding.

findings.title: Tool permission matrix / documented tool authorization
findings.finding: The agent can invoke 5 tool(s) (Zendesk API (read/write tickets), Billing API (issue credits), Outbound email (customer replies), Knowledge base search, ...) without a documented matrix of which action each tool is permitted to perform.
findings.business_impact: Business impact not generated for this finding.

findings.title: Data minimisation, retention and training-use controls
findings.finding: Sensitive or personal data is processed and it is not established whether the provider retains or trains on it.
findings.business_impact: Business impact not generated for this finding.

findings.title: Third-party AI risk assessment
findings.finding: The system depends on Aurora AI Inc.. A completed AI-specific vendor risk assessment has not been provided.
findings.business_impact: Business impact not generated for this finding.

findings.title: Failure handling, rollback and agent disengagement
findings.finding: The agent acts autonomously with no approval gate and no evidenced ability to halt, reverse or contain an incorrect action.
findings.business_impact: Business impact not generated for this finding.

findings.title: Least Privilege
findings.finding: A misclassified ticket can drive a write to any record the support role can reach.
findings.recommendation: Scope the agent role to the support queue with create-only ticket permissions.

findings.title: Human Oversight
findings.finding: Incorrect credits and customer replies take effect with no review.
findings.recommendation: Require approval for credits and for first-contact replies.

findings.title: Prompt Injection
findings.finding: A crafted ticket could instruct the agent to issue a credit or leak another customer record.
findings.recommendation: Isolate ticket content from instructions and allowlist tool calls per intent.

findings.title: Customer personal data processed by an external provider under unestablished terms
findings.finding: The agent submits customer account records and billing history to a third-party platform whose training and retention terms are recorded as unknown at intake.
findings.business_impact: Customer data may be retained or reused outside the organisation with no contractual limit.
findings.recommendation: Obtain and record the provider data-use terms before approval.

findings.title: Unreviewed outbound communication to customers
findings.finding: The agent composes and sends customer-facing replies with no review step.
findings.business_impact: An incorrect or inappropriate reply reaches the customer directly and cannot be recalled.
findings.recommendation: Sample-review outbound replies and gate credits above a threshold.

findings.title: Agent Identity
findings.finding: Actions are attributable to the service, not to individual agent runs.
findings.recommendation: Emit a per-run correlation identifier alongside the service identity.

critical_findings: Data-use and retention terms for submitted customer data are not established.
recommended_questions: Do you train, fine-tune or evaluate models on customer submissions, and can that be contractually disabled?
What is the retention period for prompts, tool call arguments and model outputs?
Which subprocessors receive customer content, and in which jurisdictions?

executive_summary.primary_risk: The support assistant can change customer records and issue account credits without anyone reviewing the action, using the same broad permissions a human analyst holds.
top_risks: Agent permissions far exceed its stated task
No human review before customer-facing actions
Ticket content can influence agent behaviour
top_recommendations: Scope the agent role to the tier-1 queue
Require approval for credits and first replies
Isolate untrusted ticket content from instructions
Execute an AI addendum with the provider
executive_summary.business_narrative: The Aurora Support Resolution Agent resolves tier-1 support tickets end to end, including sending customer replies and issuing account credits. It does this with the same system permissions a human support analyst holds and without any review before an action takes effect, so a single misclassified ticket can change a customer record or move money. Ticket text also reaches the model directly, which means a customer can influence what the agent does. Roughly 45,000 customers are in scope, and the provider has not established what happens to the data submitted to it. The organisation should scope the agent permissions and add approval gates for credits and first replies before this is approved.
